title: Networking primer for AWS
intro: VPC networking builds on IP addressing, DNS, TLS, public versus private subnet design, NAT egress, and knowing which OSI layer each AWS service operates at for systematic troubleshooting.

overviewDiagram.title: Networking primer flow
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  CIDR[IP CIDR and subnets] --> DNS[Route 53 DNS]
  DNS --> TLS[TLS certificates]
  TLS --> PUB[Public vs private]
  PUB --> NAT[NAT and routing]
  NAT --> OSI[OSI layer map]

conceptCards.title: CIDR and subnets
conceptCards.summary: /16 VPC, /24 subnets per AZ — plan non-overlapping ranges before peering.

conceptCards.title: Route 53 DNS
conceptCards.summary: ALIAS records to AWS resources; weighted routing for blue-green.
conceptCards.example: api.example.com ALIAS to ALB — no hardcoded IP.

conceptCards.title: TLS certificates
conceptCards.summary: ACM auto-renewal; terminate at ALB or CloudFront (cert in us-east-1).

conceptCards.title: Public vs private
conceptCards.summary: ALB in public; app and DB in private. SG chain between tiers.
conceptCards.example: App SG allows 8080 only from ALB SG.

conceptCards.title: NAT and gateways
conceptCards.summary: NAT per AZ for private egress; VPC endpoints for S3 to skip NAT cost.

conceptCards.title: OSI layer map
conceptCards.summary: Troubleshoot L3 routing → L4 SG → L6 TLS → L7 HTTP.
conceptCards.example: Flow Logs for REJECT; curl -v for L7.
